To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

each cloud type has a characteristic intrinsic distribution of liquid water path (with the most distinct distributions being found for low level clouds) and a diurnal cycle (with the most pronounced diurnal variations being found for low and middle cloud types).

each cloud type has a characteristic intrinsic L WP distribution that is constant in the entire SE V IRI field of view but varies for smaller regions like C entral E urope, that the relative amplitude of the LWP diurnal cycle is higher in cloudy regions than in the entire SE VIRI field of view and that the average diurnal LWP cycle is related to cloud t ype.

(i) the average LWP of low, middle, and high clouds is higher over land, (ii) the average LWC of low clouds is higher over the ocean, (iii) the average diurnal variations of LWP are larger for low and middle clouds, (iv) the average LWR is higher for low clouds, (v) the diurnal cycle of the LWP is related with the cloud type.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the temporal and spatial variations of the LWP for low, middle and upper level clouds.
the statistical properties of the LWP of different cloud types and the associated diurnal cycle.
the characteristics of cloud LWP and their relation to the cloud type.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the LWP of low and middle level cloud types are more variable in their diurnal cycle than high level clouds.
LWP is not constant in space and time and therefore the use of a constant value for the retrieval of cloud radiative forcing or the estimation of cloud feedbacks should be reconsidered.
each cloud type has a characteristic intrinsic L WP distribution and a characteristic diurnal cycle.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intrinsic diurnal variation of LWP is the dominant contributor to the overall diurnal variation.
LWP of clouds with a high liquid water content, like stratocumuli or stratiform precipitating clouds, is more variable than that of clouds with a low liquid water content, such as cirrus clouds.
the intrinsic LWP variability is a significant component of the total LWP variations and that LWP is related not only to cloud amount but also to cloud type and the geographical location.
The main takeaway from our work is that
LWP is not a constant for a given cloud type, but is highly dependent on the geographical region and the time of day.
the diurnal cycle of the LWP is driven by the diurnal cycle in the cloud cover, but that the amplitude of the LWP diurnal cycle varies with cloud type.
the diurnal cycle of the liquid water content is related to cloud types and is a function of the local time of the maximum LWP.
